deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. Page 290 derives the Pfaff-type transformation F(θ,n+θ,n+1,f²) = (1−f²)^{−θ} F(θ,1−θ,n+1,−f²/(1−f²)). Gauss compares coefficients of equal powers of f². Each coefficient reduces to a terminating series F(−k,θ,n+1,1), which he evaluates by his Π-formula. Page 291 first tries a differential-equation route to a related statement, abandons it, and returns to the coefficient route of p. 290.

(1) DEFINITION. Gauss sets
Ψ(α,β,γ,δ,x) = P = Σ_{k≥0} c_k x^k, with c_k = (α)_k(β)_k / ((γ)_k(δ)_k).
There is no k! in the denominator. So P = 3F2(α,β,1; γ,δ; x), a generalized hypergeometric series with one unit parameter. The ratio is c_{k+1}/c_k = (α+k)(β+k)/((γ+k)(δ+k)).

(2) THE OPERATOR. Gauss applies
L[P] = (αβ − (γ−1)(δ−1))P + ((α+β+1)x − (γ+δ−1))P' + (x²−x)P''.
He annotates P' and P'' as dP/dx and ddP/dx².

My computation of the coefficient of x^k in L[P]:
- It equals c_k[(α+k)(β+k) − (γ−1)(δ−1)] − c_{k+1}(k+1)(k+γ+δ−1).
- Use (k+1)(k+γ+δ−1) = (γ+k)(δ+k) − (γ−1)(δ−1).
- Use the recurrence c_{k+1}(γ+k)(δ+k) = c_k(α+k)(β+k).
- The coefficient then collapses to (γ−1)(δ−1)(c_{k+1} − c_k).

Gauss writes only the k=0 and k=1 terms:
- A = (αβ−γδ)(γ−1)(δ−1)/(γδ)
- B = αβ(γ−1)(δ−1)((α+1)(β+1) − (γ+1)(δ+1)) / (γ(γ+1)δ(δ+1))
He asserts L[P] = A + Bx. Both A and B are correct. However, the true right-hand side is the full series (γ−1)(δ−1)[(P−1)/x − P], not a binomial.

(3) SUBSTITUTION. Gauss puts x = t/(t−1), the Pfaff/Euler variable change, so that dP/dx = −(t−1)² dP/dt. After dividing by (t−1) he obtains
[αβ−(γ−1)(δ−1)]/(t−1) · P − ((α+β−γ−δ+2)t + γ+δ−1) dP/dt + (t²−t) d²P/dt² = (−A+(A+B)t)/(t−1)².
The P term, the second-derivative term and the right-hand side are right. The first-derivative coefficient is not; see errors.

(4) ABANDONMENT. He writes "Diese Art führt nicht bequem zum Ziele. Wohl aber die auf S. 290 angedeutete" (this way does not lead conveniently to the goal, but the one indicated on p. 290 does).

(5) NEW GOAL. It suffices to study the terminating series
Σ_{j=0}^{k} (−1)^j C(k,j) (1−θ)_j/(n+1)_j = 2F1(−k, 1−θ; n+1; 1),
with k a positive integer and likewise n. By Chu–Vandermonde (a special case of Gauss's summation) its sum is S = (n+θ)_k/(n+1)_k, as stated on p. 292.

The claim to be proved, continued on p. 292: if S_m is the partial sum up to the m-th term, then S − S_m always has the sign of the first omitted term. This is an enveloping, alternating-bound property. Since these coefficients are exactly what arise when the transformed series of p. 290 is re-expanded in powers of f², the aim is evidently error bounds when that series is truncated.

On p. 292 Gauss proves the case 1−θ>0. The terms alternate in sign and are unimodal in absolute value, so one argues from the front up to the largest term, then from the back.
errors: The identity L[P] = A + Bx is false as a general identity. The coefficient of x^k in L[P] is (γ−1)(δ−1)(c_{k+1}−c_k), which is nonzero for k ≥ 2 in general. Gauss's A and B are only the first two terms; the exact right-hand side is (γ−1)(δ−1)((P−1)/x − P). For instance the x² coefficient is (γ−1)(δ−1)(c_3−c_2) ≠ 0.

In the transformed equation the coefficient of dP/dt should be −((α+β−γ−δ)t + γ+δ−1), not −((α+β−γ−δ+2)t + γ+δ−1). Gauss dropped the 2(t−1)³ dP/dt contribution coming from d²P/dx², since d²P/dx² = (t−1)⁴P_tt + 2(t−1)³P_t. That contribution adds +2t(t−1)P_t after multiplying by x²−x = t/(t−1)².
Neither slip propagates: Gauss explicitly abandons this approach in the next line.

results.what: Second-order differential relation for the series Σ (α)_k(β)_k/((γ)_k(δ)_k) x^k = 3F2(α,β,1;γ,δ;x), attempted as an inhomogeneous ODE with polynomial right-hand side.
results.modern_name: Inhomogeneous second-order ODE for a 3F2 with a unit numerator parameter (generalized hypergeometric differential equation)
results.usually_credited_to: Generalized hypergeometric series: Clausen (1828), Thomae (1870); the ODE theory: Riemann, Pochhammer, Goursat

results.what: Change of variable x = t/(t−1) applied to the ODE
Sum of the terminating series 1 − k(1−θ)/(n+1) + ... = (n+θ)_k/(n+1)_k
results.usually_credited_to: Chu Shijie (1303), Vandermonde (1772); as a special case of Gauss's summation theorem (1812)

results.what: Proposed lemma: the partial sums of this terminating alternating series envelop the sum, i.e. S − S_m has the sign of the first omitted term. Used to bound truncation errors of the Pfaff-transformed series.
results.modern_name: Enveloping series / alternating-series remainder bound (Leibniz-type criterion for unimodal terms)
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz (alternating series); enveloping series studied systematically by Pólya–Szegő (1925)

deep.surprise_reason: The material is mostly standard Gauss-era hypergeometric technique: the Pfaff transformation, and Chu–Vandermonde via his own summation formula. The attempted ODE for a 3F2-type series with two denominator parameters predates Clausen and Thomae. That is mildly interesting, but it is flawed and abandoned. The enveloping-sign lemma for truncated terminating hypergeometric sums is a nice unpublished detail but elementary.

checkable.asserts: The coefficient of x^k in Gauss's L[P] equals (γ−1)(δ−1)(c_{k+1}−c_k); this should simplify to 0.
Gauss's A is correct (the constant term); this should simplify to 0.
Gauss's B is correct (the x coefficient); this should simplify to 0.
The x² coefficient of L[P] is nonzero in general, so L[P] = A + Bx is false.
The dP/dt coefficient after the substitution is −((a+b−g−d)t + g+d−1), not Gauss's −((a+b−g−d+2)t + g+d−1); the d²P/dt² coefficient is t²−t.
